title: Review Tactical Notebook — Iterative PR follow-ups
body:
Context:
- Sprint: incremental review sprint (week of 2026-02-24). Focus: reduce tail latency regressions, audit KV cache evictions, and unblock small refactors for safer rollouts.
- Repo: redwood/serving-runtime (hotpath + routing). PRs I'm juggling: #2291 (batching refactor), #2310 (kv cache heuristics).

Quick review rules (timeboxed):
- 5m: is the change narrowly scoped and does it have a clear before/after test? If no -> request smaller PR.
- 10m: grep for TODO and FIXME in changed files. If present: ask for a ticket or inline justification.
- 15m: read the test file(s) only (unit/integration); do they assert behavior or just exercise happy path? If only happy path -> ask for edge-case tests.
- 20m: smoke-run the change locally (if small): unit tests + one integration scenario. If flakey locally note signal in PR comments.

Risk signals to call out in PR comments:
- Silent performance knobs: added config flags without metrics or SLO correlation.
- Hidden cross-service effects: changes touching routing/cache that don't include an integration test in the end-to-end harness.
- Entangled refactor + feature: refactor + new behavior in same PR -> push to split or explicitly annotate rollout plan.
- Unsafe default changes: any change to DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE, cache TTLs, or eviction policy must include a canary/rollback note.

Refactor idea snippets (for follow-up PRs, short notes to self):
1) Split KV cache interface: read-optimized vs write-optimized adapters. Right now there's one path that handles both; decouple to simplify eviction tests. Low risk to split behind feature flag.
2) Make Batcher pluggable by policy type: latency-first vs throughput-first. Minimal adapter that chooses batching windows per route. Could land as an internal API change + tests.
3) Add a cheap synthetic load test that targets tail latency: use small input tokens and high QPS to ensure batching/backpressure behavior. Purpose: catch regressions in CI frequently.

Follow-ups & action items (concrete TODOs):
- [ ] INF-3012: create small canary plan for #2291 (Priya to own), include traffic split and monitor playbook (latency, error-rate, token cost).
- [ ] Break out helper functions from big utils.py in #2310 into two micro-files: eviction_policy.py + cache_metrics.py (Samir). Add unit tests for eviction edge cases.
- [ ] Add integration test in e2e-harness that simulates KV rehydrate path (Diego). Ticket INF-3120.

Questions for author to answer in PR comments (copy these as checklist in PR):
- Why this batching window was selected? Provide simple benchmark summary (p50/p95/p99 token latency).
- Are any downstream services assuming previous eviction ordering? Link to traces if so.
- If feature-flagged, what's the rollout plan and how will rollback be triggered?

Testing checklist (quick):
- Unit tests cover boundary conditions (empty input, max-length context).
- Integration test in local harness that runs at >50 QPS for 30s to surface stalls.
- CI matrix includes quantized model path (if change touches kernel selection).
- Add perf benchmark snippet in PR description with command used.

Rollback & mitigation playbook (short):
- Immediate: flip feature flag -> 5min to a config push if infra supports it.
- Short term: revert PR if regression not explained by load or infra changes. Keep revert small (only revert related files).
- Postmortem trigger: >5% tail latency regression sustained for 30+ minutes in canary -> invoke postmortem.

Common micro-comments I leave (templates):
- "Can we add a unit test for X edge-case (empty/None input)?"
- "Please add a short benchmark snippet (command + environment) used for these numbers."
- "This seems to change default behavior — can you add a customer-impact blurb and rollback plan?"

Snippets / quick commands I use when reviewing locally:
- Run unit tests for file: pytest tests/unit/test_kv_cache.py -q
- Small perf locally: ./tools/loadgen --qps 200 --seq-len 32 --model local-small --duration 30s
- Run e2e harness: ./infra/e2e/run_local.sh --scenario=kv_rehydrate --duration=60s

Loose heuristics / mental model (notes to self):
- If change touches hotpath (<10ms p50) assume high scrutiny.
- Anything that trades latency for throughput needs explicit SLO tradeoffs documented.
- Prefer many small, well-tested PRs over one big refactor. Shipability beats perfect refactor.

Misc scratch thoughts (unresolved):
- Could we add a 'trial mode' where batcher emits metrics about batching decisions for 1% of traffic? Might be useful for live instrumentation without full rollout.
- Is there an easy way to detect silent cache thrashing via traces? Might add an observability ticket.

Notes to self after pair-review with Priya (2026-03-03):
- Priya suggested adding a minimal tracing span around batch allocation; good for correlating batching windows with tail spikes. Ticket: INF-3187.
- Samir worried about test flakiness in CI due to timing; add deterministic mocks for time/sleep in unit tests.

End-of-doc capture: this is a living scratchpad. When cleaning up, copy checklist into PR descriptions and convert follow-ups to tickets. Keep this file as the canonical short-run heuristics notebook for quick reviews during this sprint.
